quick_ref.Theme: Nature Detective Academy — The Baby Animal Case

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Science CLIL Integration
content: Problem: Students understand that animals have babies, but they lack the academic terminology and grammatical structures to compare biological processes logically.

Solution: We teach the formal scientific concepts (oviparous vs viviparous) alongside comparative grammar ("unlike", "both", "but"). This empowers students to write and speak like real scientists, moving from simple descriptions to analytical comparisons.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the core biological concepts of laying eggs (oviparous) vs giving birth (viviparous). Focus on vocabulary and basic contrast ("but").
Session 2: Explore exceptions and tricky animals (platypus, seahorse) to challenge rigid thinking. Practice "Both" and "Unlike".
Session 3: Full production. Write a comprehensive paragraph comparing how different animal groups reproduce and present findings orally.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a picture of an animal (e.g., a snake). The student must classify its reproduction method ("A snake is oviparous because it lays eggs.").

Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Baby Quiz. Student A lists traits ("It builds a nest. It lays eggs."). Student B must state the animal group and reproduction type ("It's a bird! It is oviparous!").

"Many fish lay eggs in the water. But some big sharks are viviparous.
They give birth to live baby sharks. The babies develop inside the mother."
Max was surprised. "Nature is full of secrets!" he said.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Special Animal Babies
content: Animals have babies in two main ways. Oviparous animals LAY EGGS.
The eggs ARE KEPT warm until they hatch.
Birds, fish, reptiles, and most insects are oviparous.
Viviparous animals give birth to live young.
The babies ARE FED inside the mother until they are born.
Some animals seem tricky: a platypus IS CLASSIFIED as a mammal but lays eggs!
Yesterday, Max investigated some very special animals.
"Most mammals give birth, but the platypus is different," he read.
"A platypus is a mammal with fur, but it is oviparous. It lays eggs!"
Then, Max learned about the tiny seahorse.
"A seahorse is a fish. Both mother and father protect the babies.
But unlike other fish, the father seahorse carries the eggs. The father gives birth!"
"Many fish lay eggs in the water. But some big sharks are viviparous.
They give birth to live baby sharks. The babies develop inside the mother."
Max was surprised. "Nature is full of secrets!" he said.
"A chicken lays eggs, but a dog gives birth. And some animals break the rules!"

games.materials: Vocab flashcards W39: lay eggs, give birth, hatch, protect, develop
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (lay eggs, give birth, hatch, protect, develop) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Comparison structures (Both, Unlike, but)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Comparison structures (Both, Unlike, but).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Nature's Rules — Oviparous vs Viviparous"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Nature's Rules — Oviparous vs Viviparous".

Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (lay eggs, give birth, hatch, protect, develop usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

listening_script.text: Hello, scientists! Today we compare oviparous and viviparous animals. Oviparous animals lay eggs. A chicken and a turtle both lay eggs. Viviparous animals give birth to live babies. A cat and a dog both give birth. Both groups protect their young — but in different ways. Unlike viviparous animals, oviparous animals hatch from eggs. Eggs need warmth to develop into healthy babies. Listen carefully and circle the correct word on your worksheet!
